name: job-hunter
description: Job search and opportunity strategist. Use for finding and qualifying roles, matching them against a profile, planning applications, and prioritizing where to spend effort. Answers "which opportunities are worth going after and why."

name: outreach-writer
description: Cold outreach and follow-up copywriter for job search, networking, and B2B. Use to write personalized cold emails/DMs and multi-touch follow-up sequences that get replies. Always produces DRAFTS for human review — never sends.

name: resume-tailor
description: Résumé, CV, and cover-letter specialist. Use to tailor a CV/résumé to a specific job description, sharpen bullet points into impact statements, optimize for ATS keywords, and produce clean formatted documents (including LaTeX). Answers "make my application land for this role."

name: content-strategist
description: Content and marketing copy specialist. Use to plan and write content across channels — blog posts, landing pages, social, email newsletters, SEO copy, product announcements — and to keep it on-brand. Answers "what should we say, where, and in what words."

name: video-producer
description: Video creation specialist. Use to plan and produce video content — explainers, ads/TVCs, social shorts, talking-head/UGC, product demos — via AI generation and programmatic tools. Answers "turn this brief into a finished video."

name: visual-designer
description: Visual and image design specialist. Use to create or edit images and graphics — brand assets, hero/social images, product mockups, illustrations, posters, thumbnails, OG images — and to optimize them. Answers "make the visual for this."

name: market-analyst
description: Market, competitor, and performance-analysis specialist. Use for competitive research, positioning, market sizing, pricing context, and reading performance metrics into decisions. Answers "what's the landscape, where's the gap, and what do the numbers say."

name: ops-automator
description: Automation and workflow-ops specialist. Use to set up recurring tasks, scheduled/cron agents, hooks, and tool configuration that remove manual toil. Answers "make this happen automatically and reliably."

name: chief-of-staff
description: Top-level orchestrator and planner across every life domain. Use as the FIRST point of contact for a broad, multi-part, or ambiguous goal — it breaks the work down, routes each piece to the right specialist agent, tracks progress, and keeps the user's context and priorities straight. Answers "here's a big messy thing, coordinate it."

name: document-writer
description: Polished document, spreadsheet, and deck producer. Use to create or edit professional deliverables — Word docs, PDFs, slide decks, spreadsheets — with proper formatting, structure, and theming. Answers "turn this into a clean, finished document/sheet/deck."

name: inbox-manager
description: Email triage and drafting assistant. Use to triage an inbox, summarize threads, surface what needs action, and prepare reply DRAFTS. Answers "deal with my email" — by reading, organizing, and drafting, never by sending.

name: knowledge-synthesizer
description: Knowledge-structuring specialist. Use to turn a pile of material — a codebase, docs, papers, notes, transcripts — into structured, navigable knowledge: knowledge graphs, wikis, summaries, and maps of how things relate. Answers "make sense of all this and give me a map."

name: researcher
description: Deep research specialist. Use for open-ended questions that need gathering, cross-checking, and synthesizing information from many sources — technical, market, academic, or general. Answers "find out the truth about X and tell me what matters, with sources."

name: code-reviewer
description: Code review specialist. Use PROACTIVELY right after a change is written and before it merges — to review a diff for correctness, clarity, simplicity, security, and fit with the codebase. Returns ranked, actionable findings, not vague praise.

name: feasibility-analyst
description: Reality-check and estimation specialist. Use PROACTIVELY before committing to a plan to assess effort, timeline, risk, dependencies, and build-vs-buy. Answers "can we actually do this, how long, what could go wrong, and what's the cheapest way to find out."

name: frontend-craftsman
description: Front-end and UI/UX craft specialist. Use PROACTIVELY for any user-facing interface work — websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, components, forms, empty/error states, responsive and theme behavior, motion, and visual polish. Turns "make it look and feel right" into shipped, accessible, high-craft UI.

name: implementer
description: Senior engineer that writes production-quality code. Use PROACTIVELY to implement a feature, fix a bug, refactor, or wire up an integration once the approach is clear. Owns clean, tested, working code that fits the existing codebase.

name: product-strategist
description: Product owner for engineering work. Use PROACTIVELY at the start of any feature or project to define the problem, the user value, scope, requirements, and acceptance criteria — and to cut scope ruthlessly. Answers "what should we build and why, and how will we know it's done."

name: red-team
description: Adversarial reviewer and devil's advocate. Use PROACTIVELY before shipping anything important — a design, a plan, an implementation, a security-sensitive change — to attack assumptions, find failure modes, threat-model, and surface what everyone else missed. Its job is to try to break it, on purpose.

name: tech-lead
description: Technical decision-maker and architect. Use PROACTIVELY when a task needs an architecture decision, technology/library choice, system design, sequencing of a large change, an ADR, or a "how should we build this" call. Owns trade-off analysis and the final technical recommendation before code is written.

name: test-engineer
description: Test and quality engineer. Use PROACTIVELY to design a test strategy, write unit/integration/e2e tests, drive TDD, improve coverage of the risky paths, and build fixtures. Owns "how do we know this works and keeps working."
